channel.title: East & Inner with Ollie
channel.description: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern ear. No jargon. No mysticism. Just the real stuff — from the Huangdi Neijing to your morning coffee. Hosted by Ollie, a lifelong student of Chinese medicine who reads the classics so you don't have to. New episodes every other week.
channel.itunes:author: Ollie
channel.itunes:summary: Classical Chinese medicine, translated for the modern ear. No jargon. No mysticism. Just the real stuff — from the Huangdi Neijing to your morning coffee.

item.title: Ep11: Li Qiu — Why the First Day of Autumn Makes the Chinese Reach for Pears
item.description: On a hot August day, the Chinese calendar says autumn has begun — and families are eating hearty meat on purpose. Why Li Qiu matters, how Autumn Dryness targets the Lungs, and why pears, lily bulb, and white fungus are the season's perfect answer. Includes the classic pear soup recipe. Based on TCM Way blog #44.
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep10: Why Your Acupuncturist Hasn't Told You About Moxibustion
item.description: Acupuncture is only half of an ancient medicine. The other half is moxibustion — warming the body with a smoldering herb called mugwort. Why your acupuncturist probably never mentions it, what a session actually feels like, and what the classics and modern research say about it. Based on TCM Way blog #46. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/46-why-your-acupuncturist-hasnt-told-you-about-moxibustion.html 🟠 Medium: https://medium.com/@tcmway/why-your-acupuncturist-hasnt-told-you-about-moxibustion-3ed5c3d973db
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep09: The Season of Letting Go — What the Neijing Knew About Autumn
item.description: The oak in the park doesn't fight autumn — it lets go. The Neijing's radical prescription for this season: don't start up — let go. Discover Rong Ping, why autumn belongs to Metal and the Lungs, why grief has its season, and why letting go is the most practical thing you can do before winter. Based on TCM Way blog #42. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/42-the-season-of-letting-go-autumn-neijing.html 🟠 Medium: https://medium.com/@tcmway/the-season-of-letting-go-what-the-neijing-knew-about-autumn-42c06778ff93
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep08: Your Anxiety Is Not in Your Head
item.description: Why does your anxiety keep coming back no matter how many meditation apps you try? Chinese medicine has a different answer — and it's not in your brain. It's in your Liver. Discover Liver Qi Stagnation: the traffic jam inside your body that explains the sighs, the 2 AM wake-ups, and the PMS you thought was just your lot in life. Based on TCM Way blog #32. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/32-your-anxiety-is-not-in-your-head-understanding-the-liver-qi-connection.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep07: The Season Your Body Is Actually In
item.description: It was the third week of July and my wife told me I'd been a jerk all week. Turns out, it wasn't the heat — it was my Heart. Discover the five seasons your body secretly lives by, why summer makes you snap, and how a simple flower tea changed everything. Based on TCM Way blog #35. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/35-the-season-your-body-is-actually-in.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep01: Yin & Yang ≠ Good vs Evil
item.description: The biggest mistranslation in the history of wellness culture: Yin and Yang are NOT good and evil. Ollie walks you through the seesaw, the three rules nobody told you, and why you should stop driving nails through your internal balance. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/16-yin-yang-not-good-vs-evil.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep02: Stop Fighting, Start Warming
item.description: When a cold hits, your first instinct is to fight it. But Chinese medicine says that's exactly the wrong move. Discover the three warming herbs — Gui Zhi, Gan Jiang, and Fu Zi — and learn why your body doesn't need a warrior. It just needs a blanket. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/21-stop-fighting-start-warming.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep03: Traffic Jam — Why Your Emotions Get Stuck
item.description: You're stuck. Irritable. Everything feels like too much. Classical Chinese medicine calls this Liver Qi stagnation — your internal traffic is gridlocked. Ollie explains the highway inside your body and why emotions really do get stuck. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/04-traffic-jam-inside-your-body.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep04: What Is Qi, Actually?
item.description: You've heard the word a thousand times. But what IS Qi, actually? Not the wellness-industry version — the real thing. Ollie explains the five functions of Qi, the four ways it goes wrong, and why your body has been trying to tell you something your whole life. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/03-qi-is-not-magic.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep05: Food Temperature — Why Your Body Doesn't Want That Salad
item.description: Every wellness influencer tells you to eat more salads. But some bodies don't want cold food — they want warmth. Ollie explains the forgotten wisdom of food temperature, the digestive fire, and why Chinese medicine has been warning about cold foods for two thousand years. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/34-eat-with-the-sun-the-tcm-clock-for-food.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie

item.title: Ep06: Fear Lives in Your Kidneys — The Emotion-Organ Map
item.description: Every emotion has an address in the body. Anger lives in the liver. Joy in the heart. And fear — deep, chronic, background fear — lives in the kidneys. Ollie shares the ancient Five Element organ-emotion map, a personal story about Kidney energy depletion, and why going to bed before 11 PM might be the most profound thing you can do for your fear. 📖 文字版: https://tcmway.net/posts/17-five-elements-not-personality-test.html
item.itunes:author: Ollie
